metas.name: Bunya Pine
metas.note: The Bunya pine's natural range is southeast Queensland. There are many planted specimens throughout the world due to its very aesthetic appearance.
metas.footer: Click -> Araucaria Bidwillii for more information!

metas.name: Dahurian Larch
metas.note: The Dahurian Larch is a species of larch native to eastern Siberia and adjacent northeastern Mongolia, South Korea, and other countries not featured in Geoguessr.
metas.footer: Click -> Larix gmelinii for more information!

metas.name: Douglas Fir
metas.note: The Douglas fir is native to western North America and despite its common names, it is not a true fir, spruce, or pine. It's a "false hemlock".
metas.footer: Click -> Pseudotsuga Menziesii for more information!

metas.name: Jack Pine
metas.note: Jack pines are found in Canada mostly anywhere east of the Rockies, but in US they can actually be really good to regionguess since they mostly grow from Minnesota to Maine, almost always on sandy and rocky soil. Their scraggly, irregular shape is similar to the Pitch pine. However their distribution is very similar to the Red pine (P. Resinosa).
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Banksiana for more information!

metas.name: Khasi Pine
metas.note: The Khasi Pine's range extends from Meghalaya India to northern Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, and most noticeably in the Luzon tropical pine forests of the Philippines where it is also known as the Benguet Pine. (I excluded non-geoguessr countries from the list).
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Kesiya for more information!

metas.name: Loblolly Pine
metas.note: Pinus taeda, commonly known as Loblolly pine, is one of several pines native to the Southeastern United States. It can be easily mistaken with the Red pine (P. Resinosa) since they both have clumps of needles at the end of the branch, however, the clumps from the Loblolly appear bigger in size and less "rounded" compared to the Red pine. The clumps of the Red pine when seen from afar look dark green or even black.
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Taeda for more information!

metas.name: Monkey Puzzle
metas.note: The closest relative to the Paraná Pine, this tree's native habitat is the lower slopes of the Chilean and Argentine south-central Andes.
metas.footer: Click -> Araucaria Araucana for more information!

metas.name: Parana Pine
metas.note: Besides southern Brazil, it is also found in high-altitude areas of southern Minas Gerais, in central Rio de Janeiro and in the east and south of São Paulo, but more typically in the states of Paraná, Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.
metas.footer: Click -> Araucaria Angustifolia for more information!

metas.name: Pitch Pine
metas.note: Pitch pine is found mainly in the southern areas of the northeastern United States, from coastal Maine and Ohio to Kentucky and northern Georgia.
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Rigida for more information!

metas.name: Red Pine
metas.note: Pinus resinosa, known as red pine (also Norway pine in Minnesota), is a pine native to Eastern North America, with a similar distribution to the Jack pines (P. Banksiana). It can be easily mistaken with the Loblolly pine (P. Taeda) since they both have clumps of needles at the end of the branch, however, the clumps from the Red pine appear "rounded" and smaller in size compared to those from the Loblolly pine. The clumps of the Red pine when seen from afar look dark green or even black.
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Resinosa for more information!

metas.name: Scots Pine
metas.note: The Scots Pine / Baltic pine / European Red Pine is a species of tree in the pine family Pinaceae that is native to Eurasia. The best use for it in Geoguessr is to clear a possible confusion between North America and Europe / Russia.
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Sylvestris for more information!

metas.name: Stone Pine
metas.note: The tree is native to the Mediterranean region, occurring in Southern Europe and the Levant. The species was introduced into North Africa millennia ago, and is also naturalized in the Canary Islands, South Africa and New South Wales.
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Pinea for more information!

metas.name: Sumatran Pine
metas.note: The Sumatran pine, is a pine native to the Malesia region of southeast Asia, and the only one that occurs naturally south of the equator. It is found mainly in North Sumatra and Java (rarely in Sulawesi) and also in Philippines in Mindoro and Palawan.
metas.footer: Click -> Pinus Merkusii for more information!
